div.p: The Nausikaa episode is finished this morning – 4. a.m. Will be typed and sent in a few days. Have been ill but am now better. Hope you are well.

div.note: The face of this postcard reproduces a painting, captioned on the reverse, “TRIESTE - Piazza grande dal mare.” The artist is Edoardo Marchioro (1882-1935), born in Schio, near Vicenza. He painted many scenes of Trieste, Trento, and other cities that were reproduced on postcards. Marchioro trained at La Scala, the opera house in Milan, and from the 1920s was noted for the scene designs he created for productions there, including Verdi’s Otello and Forza del destino and Puccini’s Tosca. His career is discussed in Giuseppe Adami, Edoardo Marchioro: Pittore, scenografo del Teatro alla Scala (Milan: Emilio Bestetti, 1945), and Giovanna Grossato, Edoardo Marchioro, pittore e scenografo della Scala (Edizioni Livio Greselin, 1976). Marchioro’s 1917 painting of the Piazza Grande (Great Square, later renamed Piazza Unità d’Italia) shows one of the busiest areas of Trieste, facing the Adriatic Sea, with its magisterial commercial buildings, palaces, wooded area, and San Giusto castle on the hill behind.

“Nausicaa,” the thirteenth episode of Ulysses, appeared in three numbers of The Little Review, vol. 6, no. 11-vol. 7, nos. 1-2 (April, May-June, July-August 1920): 43-50, 61-72, 42-58. The portion in the July-August 1920 number, containing the scene of Leopold Bloom’s masturbation at the seashore, caused the editors Margaret Caroline Anderson (1886-1973) and Jane Heap (1883-1964) to be prosecuted for publishing obscenity; they were convicted and fined $50 each by a New York court in 1921. For a fuller account, see JJ to Pound, 24 October 1919, notes.

As JJ completed episodes of Ulysses, he had copies typed and sent to Pound, who reviewed and transmitted them to New York for serial publication in The Little Review, and to Harriet Shaw Weaver (1876-1961), editor of The Egoist in London. Because of English printers’ fears, The Egoist never consistently serialized Ulysses, and published only a few episodes: “Nestor,” “Proteus,” “Hades,” and part of “Wandering Rocks.”
